Derivation: exact mean and variance of the bivariate cross nearest-neighbour G function

Source: vignettes/derivation-bivariate.Rmd
derivation-bivariate.Rmd

This vignette proves the closed-form mean and variance of the bivariate cross nearest-neighbour statistic under a disjoint label-permutation null, again without reference to code. The univariate result of the companion vignette is recovered as the special case .

Remark 5 (the mean depends only on ). The type- count enters Theorem 3 only through the prefactor , so it cancels: the expected cross- curve is unchanged if changes, as long as , and hence the type- mark, is fixed. This asymmetry is intuitive: how many type- points there are does not change the chance that a given one finds a type- neighbour. It is also visible in the implementation, where only enters the avoidance table.

5. The diagonal case

When the two marks coincide, the natural reading of is the univariate nearest-neighbour statistic computed on a uniform subset of size : there is no independent . The package implements by delegating to the univariate estimator with , and Theorems 1–2 then apply verbatim. This is the correct reduction because in the univariate problem the neighbour of a marked point may be any other marked point, whereas in Lemma 7 and are disjoint.

6. Numerical illustration

For small patterns the bivariate null can be enumerated exhaustively: for each of the choices of , run over all choices of from the remaining locations. With , and this is configurations.

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(permfreeG))
set.seed(11)
N <- 10; ni <- 4; nj <- 3
x <- stats::runif(N); y <- stats::runif(N)
radii <- seq(0, 1.2, by = 0.15)

D <- as.matrix(stats::dist(cbind(x, y)))
ci <- utils::combn(N, ni)
Gsim <- NULL
for (j in seq_len(ncol(ci))) {
  Si <- ci[, j]
  rem <- setdiff(seq_len(N), Si)
  cj <- utils::combn(length(rem), nj)
  for (k in seq_len(ncol(cj))) {
    Sj <- rem[cj[, k]]
    Gsim <- rbind(Gsim,
                  vapply(radii, function(rr)
                    mean(rowSums(D[Si, Sj, drop = FALSE] <= rr) > 0), numeric(1)))
  }
}

d <- data.frame(x = x, y = y,
                m = factor(c(rep("A", ni), rep("B", nj),
                             rep("C", N - ni - nj))))
res <- as.data.frame(exact_gcross(d, radii = radii, mark_col = "m",
                                  marks_i = "A", marks_j = "B"))

c(max_mean_error     = max(abs(res$csr_mean - colMeans(Gsim))),
  max_variance_error = max(abs(res$csr_var -
                               apply(Gsim, 2,
                                     function(z) mean((z - mean(z))^2)))))
#>     max_mean_error max_variance_error 
#>       3.330669e-16       2.359224e-16

Again the errors are pure floating-point round-off.

A direct check of Remark 5 is also immediate: changing while holding fixed leaves the exact mean unchanged.

pp <- spatstat.geom::ppp(x, y,
                         window = spatstat.geom::owin(range(x), range(y)),
                         marks = d$m)
a <- permfreeG:::csr_cross_moments_cpp(x, y, radii, 4L, nj)
b <- permfreeG:::csr_cross_moments_cpp(x, y, radii, 5L, nj)
max(abs(a$mean - b$mean))
#> [1] 0
